## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode #13944: clickable terminal links — emit OSC 8 escape sequences around URIs in TUI tool output (SMALL priority, new feature)

- **What**: Kilocode TUI now wraps URIs in tool output with OSC 8 escape sequences (`\x1b]8;;URI\x1b\\text\x1b]8;;\x1b\\`), so terminals that support OSC 8 (iTerm2, WezTerm, Windows Terminal, VS Code terminal, Hyper, Alacritty 0.11+) render them as clickable hyperlinks. Detects HTTP/HTTPS URLs, file:// URIs, and file:line patterns (e.g. `src/foo.ts:42`) in bash stdout/stderr, error messages, and tool results. The same text is printed for non-supporting terminals (the escape sequences are ignored), so backward compatibility is maintained.
- **Why**: Tool output frequently contains URIs (file paths from grep, URLs from webfetch, file:line from lint errors). Without OSC 8, users must manually copy-paste to open them. Clickable links reduce friction (one click vs copy, switch window, paste, enter).
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13944 (feat(cli): make terminal links clickable)
- **Category**: command (TUI rendering)
- **Size**: SMALL priority, ~2h. Alexi's TUI (src/cli/tui/) already syntax-highlights bash output (via cli-highlight, per 032-tui-exact-clone) but does NOT emit OSC 8 for URIs. Add a link-detection pass in the tool-output renderer (likely src/cli/tui/components/MessageContent.tsx or the bash/grep/glob tool output formatters): regex match `https?://[^\s]+`, `file://[^\s]+`, and `[a-zA-Z0-9/_.-]+:[0-9]+` (file:line patterns like `src/foo.ts:42`), wrap each in OSC 8 `\x1b]8;;URI\x1b\\text\x1b]8;;\x1b\\`. For file:line patterns, construct a file:// URI with the absolute path and line fragment (e.g. `file:///absolute/path/src/foo.ts#42`). Test by running `ax chat -m "list all TypeScript files"` or `ax chat -m "grep for 'export' in src/"` and confirming file paths are clickable in a supporting terminal (iTerm2, WezTerm, Windows Terminal). Verify non-supporting terminals (e.g. basic xterm) still print the text without mangling.

#### 2. Kilocode #13969: mistake-limit user prompt — ask user how to continue when loop detector or mistake tracker trips (MODERATE priority, UX improvement)

- **What**: When the loop detector (5 identical consecutive tool calls) or mistake tracker (6 consecutive failures) trips, Kilocode now routes the decision to the user via onConsecutiveMistakeLimitReached callback: "Try a different approach" / "Stop this run". On "continue", the agent steers guidance into the running turn explaining the loop/mistake and asking the model to try a different approach. Previously the SDK default "stop" applied and the run ended silently, so users saw the agent "randomly stop" mid-task with no explanation. The identical-call counter survives across turns, so a nudge without this fix dies after one more call.
- **Why**: Loop/mistake tripping is not a fatal error — the model may recover with steering. Silent stops are confusing (users cannot tell if it is a bug, a timeout, or a deliberate stop) and require manual nudges that re-trigger the loop. An interactive prompt gives the user agency and surfaces the reason for the pause.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13969 (fix(desktop): ask the user how to continue when the mistake limit trips instead of stopping silently)
- **Category**: command (orchestrator loop handling, TUI prompt)
- **Size**: MODERATE priority, ~4h. Alexi's orchestrator (src/core/orchestrator.ts, src/core/streamingOrchestrator.ts) does NOT register onConsecutiveMistakeLimitReached, so the SDK default "stop" applies and users experience silent stops. Add the callback: in interactive mode (ax chat, ax agent), route the decision through the TUI question component (existing `question` tool pattern already handles user prompts, see src/tool/tools/question.ts and src/cli/tui/components/ for the UI surface). On "Try a different approach", inject steering guidance into the running turn — either via a synthetic user message appended to the conversation ("The last 5 tool calls were identical, suggesting a loop. Please try a different approach.") or via a streaming injection if the orchestrator supports mid-turn steering. On "Stop this run", abort the turn gracefully (existing abort path). Wire the callback into both orchestrator.ts and streamingOrchestrator.ts (check which one is used for ax chat vs ax agent). Test by creating a mock tool that always returns the same result, calling it 6 times in a row, and confirming the user is prompted instead of the run stopping silently. Verify the steering message reaches the model on "continue" and the next call differs.

#### 3. Kilocode #13960: home-directory index guard — refuse to build file index when workspace root is home directory or filesystem root (SMALL priority, safety guard)

- **What**: Kilocode's file index (used by @ mentions and context search) now refuses to build an index when the workspace root is the home directory or filesystem root, because indexing every file under $HOME can take the process to many GB of RSS and get it OOM-killed. The guard compares realpaths (so symlinked or differently-cased spellings of the home directory still hit the guard) and skips indexing entirely (no partial index, no warning-and-proceed). Users running `kilo` from $HOME or `/` see a clear error message when attempting an @ mention or file search.
- **Why**: Users who run the CLI from $HOME (common when testing or when the default shell directory is $HOME) and type an @ mention can OOM-kill the process (GitHub issue #13930, #13905 report 10+ GB RSS and OOM crashes). The file index lists every file under the workspace root and the mention picker re-ranks the whole index on each keystroke. Without the guard, the first @ mention in $HOME can freeze the terminal for minutes and exhaust system memory.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13960 (fix(core): do not build a file index for the home directory or filesystem root)
- **Category**: tool (glob, codesearch, filesystem safety)
- **Size**: SMALL priority, ~1h. Alexi does NOT have this guard. src/tool/tools/glob.ts, src/tool/tools/codesearch.ts, and src/core/filesystem/ may trigger full-workspace scans. Add a guard in the glob/codesearch entry points (and any other code that walks the workspace recursively): before starting the scan, resolve the workspace root via `fs.realpathSync` and compare it to the home directory (`process.env.HOME || process.env.USERPROFILE || require('os').homedir()`) and filesystem root (`path.parse(workspaceRoot).root`). If it matches either, throw a clear error: "Indexing the home directory or filesystem root is disabled to prevent OOM. Please cd into a project directory." Test by running `ax chat` from $HOME (outside any repo) and attempting a glob pattern (`*.ts`) or @ mention (if Alexi has @ mention support) — confirm the error message appears immediately and the process does not balloon in memory. Also test from `/` (filesystem root) on Linux/macOS and `C:\` on Windows.

#### 4. Kilocode #13927: /caffeinate command — prevent OS sleep during long runs (LOW priority, platform-specific)

- **What**: Kilocode now has a `/caffeinate` command (desktop and CLI) that prevents the OS from sleeping during long agent runs. On macOS it calls `caffeinate -d` (display awake), on Windows `SetThreadExecutionState(ES_CONTINUOUS | ES_DISPLAY_REQUIRED)`, on Linux it uses systemd-inhibit or xdg-screensaver if available. The command is a toggle (on/off); state is shown in the status bar (desktop) or in the prompt (CLI).
- **Why**: Overnight or multi-hour runs can be interrupted by OS sleep or display sleep. Without caffeinate, users must manually disable sleep in system settings and remember to re-enable it afterwards.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13927 (feat(cli): add /caffeinate command)
- **Category**: command (CLI command, OS integration)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi has no /caffeinate command. This is a convenience feature for long-running unattended sessions. Defer until user demand surfaces (no GitHub issues requesting it). Keep on radar for future CLI commands work.

#### 5. Kilocode #13945: snapshot progress session hang fix — prevent snapshot initialization from blocking session start (LOW priority, snapshot-specific)

- **What**: Kilocode's snapshot initialization (loading workspace snapshots for session resume) was blocking session start when the snapshot read was slow (large repos, slow disk). Fix moves snapshot initialization to a background task and allows the session to start immediately with a "loading snapshot..." indicator.
- **Why**: Blocking on snapshot load makes the UI unresponsive (spinner freezes, user cannot cancel) for 5-10 seconds in large repos. Background loading keeps the UI interactive.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13945 (fix(cli): prevent snapshot progress session hangs)
- **Category**: config (snapshot loading, async initialization)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi's snapshot system (src/core/snapshot.ts) may have the same issue, but no user reports of slow snapshot initialization blocking session start. Defer until a concrete bug report surfaces. If Alexi adds snapshot loading in the future, follow Kilocode's async pattern.

#### 6. Kilocode #13942: goal replacement fix — allow goals to replace running responses (LOW priority, goal-specific)

- **What**: Kilocode's goal system (long-running multi-turn tasks) now allows a new goal to replace a running response (the previous goal's reply is aborted and the new goal starts immediately). Previously a new goal sent while a response was streaming queued behind it, causing confusion (user sends a new goal to cancel/redirect, but the old response continues streaming).
- **Why**: Goals are high-level task instructions; when a user sends a new goal mid-response, they are signaling that the current response is wrong or obsolete. Queueing the new goal behind the old response is counter-intuitive (the user must wait for the wrong response to finish before the correction starts).
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13942 (fix(goal): allow goals to replace running responses)
- **Category**: command (goal system, turn management)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi has no goal system (no src/core/goal.ts or goal-related commands). This is Kilocode-specific. Not immediately actionable.

#### 8. Kilocode #13925: console bundle size optimization — reduce startup bundle size (LOW priority, web console-specific)

- **What**: Kilocode's web console (kilo-console) reduced its startup bundle size by code-splitting heavy dependencies (marked, react-markdown, syntax highlighters) and lazy-loading them on demand. Startup bundle dropped from ~800 KB to ~400 KB.
- **Why**: Large startup bundles delay time-to-interactive on slow networks. Code-splitting moves non-critical code to secondary chunks that load after the main UI is interactive.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13925 (fix(kilo-console): reduce startup bundle size)
- **Category**: config (build optimization, web console)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi has no web console, no startup bundle (it is a CLI). This is web-console-specific. Not CLI-portable.

#### 12. Kilocode #13970: editor old_text recovery guidance — improve error message when editor old_text is null/omitted (SMALL priority, already covered by 2026-09-08 #13835 apply_patch guard)

- **What**: Kilocode's editor tool (src/tool/tools/editor.ts or equivalent) now shows a clearer error message when old_text is null or omitted for an existing file: "old_text is required for UPDATE operations on existing files. If you are creating a new file, omit old_text or use insert_line. If you are updating an existing file, re-read the file to get the current old_text." Previously the error was terse ("old_text is required") and did not explain how to recover, so models that fill optional parameters with null (observed with cline-pass/kimi-k3) re-sent the identical call until the loop detector stopped the run.
- **Why**: Clear recovery guidance reduces loop frequency. Models that see "old_text is required" with no context may retry with the same null value; models that see "re-read the file to get the current old_text" know what to do next.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13970 (fix(tools): tell the model how to recover when editor old_text is null)
- **Category**: tool (editor, error messaging)
- **Size**: SMALL priority, DEFER. Alexi has apply_patch (src/tool/tools/apply-patch.ts) and edit (src/tool/tools/edit.ts), NOT editor. The equivalent issue (null old_text or missing old_text) is already covered by 2026-09-08's item #20 (Kilocode #13835 apply_patch overwrite guard), which verifies that apply_patch refuses to overwrite existing files during Add File operations. If Alexi's edit tool has a similar null-parameter issue, add recovery guidance to the error message following this pattern. Defer until a concrete loop report surfaces. Keep on radar for error-message improvements.

#### 13. Kilocode #13976 + #13968: observer stream deduplication and busy-run gate — prevent observer client from doubling streamed chat chunks (MODERATE priority, hub-specific)

- **What**: Kilocode's sidecar (the local bridge between the desktop UI and the core agent runtime) has two hub sockets that both receive a session's events: ClineCore's own client and the hub observer client. Both were emitting the same streamed deltas, so for a session streaming through the hub every delta was emitted twice (duplicated assistant text, duplicated tool rows). Fix #13968 adds a per-stream arbitration: the first source to deliver a contended stream wins and the other is muted until the owner falls silent for 5s; also stamps each chunk with the sidecar's boot id so a process restart does not cause the replay guard to drop the new process's stream. Fix #13976 hardens the busy-run gate: while the session is busy, the observer stream stands down regardless of silence duration (the 5s window only governs idle sessions), and the core-pipe liveness mark is cleared on every sidecar stop path (stop command, provider-change rebuild, reset) so a later run on the same session does not inherit the previous run's mark.
- **Why**: Duplicated deltas broke live rendering (assistant text appeared twice, tool rows stuck at "start" until the turn-end reconcile, user message bubbles vanished mid-turn). The bug only showed on sessions that streamed without a local send first (a run already in flight when the task was opened, a resumed or scheduled run).
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13976 (fix(desktop): keep the observer stream stood down for the whole busy run), https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13968 (fix(desktop): stop the live chat stream from doubling and dropping chunks)
- **Category**: config (hub client, streaming deduplication)
- **Size**: MODERATE priority, SKIP. Alexi has no sidecar, no hub observer client, no dual-socket streaming architecture. This is Kilocode desktop-app-specific (their architecture separates the UI from the runtime via a sidecar; Alexi is a single-process CLI). Not CLI-portable.

#### 14. Kilocode SDK #13519: authenticated remote Hub connections — support auth headers for remote hub connections (MODERATE priority, hub SDK-specific)

- **What**: Kilocode SDK (the core agent runtime library) now supports authenticated remote Hub connections via custom HTTP headers (Authorization, x-api-key, etc.). Previously the Hub connection was localhost-only with no auth; this change allows the SDK to connect to a remote Hub (e.g. a cloud-hosted Hub, a Hub behind a reverse proxy) with bearer tokens or API keys. The auth headers are passed via a new `hub.auth` config option in the SDK client constructor.
- **Why**: Remote Hub deployments (multi-tenant cloud Hubs, enterprise Hubs behind SSO) need authentication. Localhost-only Hubs are fine for local development but cannot scale to team/fleet deployments.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13519 (feat(sdk): support authenticated remote Hub connections)
- **Category**: config (hub client, authentication)
- **Size**: MODERATE priority, SKIP. Alexi has no Hub (no src/core/hub.ts or hub-related client code). This is Kilocode SDK-specific. Not immediately actionable. If Alexi adds a Hub in the future, consider authenticated remote connections from the start.

#### 15. Kilocode #13887 + #13886: root session history filtering and imported session provenance — improve session listing and imported session tracking (LOW priority, session management)

- **What**: Two session-management improvements: (1) #13887 adds a rootOnly filter to the session list API (SQL WHERE on is_subagent / parent_session_id) so listing history no longer over-fetches subagent rows and then drops them client-side (one session with 2000+ child rows could hide all root sessions), (2) #13886 stamps imported sessions (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex imports) with a sessionHistoryOrigin { mode: "import", trigger: <tool> } marker that persists across resumes and is propagated to telemetry (session_origin, session_origin_trigger), so imported transcripts can be filtered separately from native sessions.
- **Why**: (1) Over-fetching child rows hits the 2000-row cap, making the desktop sidebar render empty history with no way to load more. (2) Imported sessions keep the source agent's tool names and schemas, so they behave worse on resume than native sessions; tagging them allows telemetry to separate import-related errors from native-session errors and allows the UI to show import warnings.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13887 (fix(core): keep root sessions in history when child rows crowd the scan window), https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13886 (feat(core): mark imported sessions with an import history origin and stamp it on telemetry)
- **Category**: config (session listing, import tracking)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi does NOT have session import (no src/core/session-import.ts or import-related code), no subagent parent/child hierarchy (no is_subagent field in session storage), no telemetry with session_origin stamping. These are Kilocode-specific session-management features. Defer until Alexi adds session import or subagent support.

#### 16. Kilocode #13964: imported session warnings — warn in chat and summarize foreign history on resume (MODERATE priority, import-specific)

- **What**: Imported sessions (Claude Code, Codex, opencode transcripts) now show a warning banner in the chat view naming the source tool and explaining that resuming may behave worse than a native session. When a marked-import session is resumed, the core runs a manual agentic compaction over the whole foreign history (summarizing the transcript in 1-2 paragraphs) before the first model request, so the model works from a summary instead of raw foreign-tool calls. The summary is ephemeral (lives in the sidecar, not persisted to the canonical transcript), and the "Thinking..." indicator reads "Summarizing the imported <tool> history..." while it runs.
- **Why**: Imported transcripts keep the source agent's tool names and schemas, which the model may try to call (e.g. a Claude Code transcript has `editFile` calls; if the model tries to call `editFile` in Kilocode, it fails because Kilocode's tool is `editor`). Summarizing the foreign history on resume prevents the model from copying foreign tool names.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13964 (Imported sessions: warn in the chat and summarize the foreign history on resume)
- **Category**: config (session import, compaction)
- **Size**: MODERATE priority, SKIP. Alexi does NOT have session import (no src/core/session-import.ts or import-related code). This is Kilocode-specific. Defer until Alexi adds session import support. If session import is added in the future, follow Kilocode's pattern: warn users about imported sessions and summarize foreign history on resume.

#### 17. Kilocode #13971: session-history usage pagination — hydrate token/cost for visible page, not just first four rows (LOW priority, UI pagination)

- **What**: Kilocode desktop app's session-history view now hydrates token usage and cost for the visible page of sessions (up to 10 rows at a time, on demand as the user pages through history) instead of hard-coding the first four rows. Previously every row beyond the first four rendered "-" for tokens and cost, and paging never asked for more. Transcript reads are capped at four in flight (each one parses a whole session file), and a session whose status changed while its usage read was pending is re-read with the new status.
- **Why**: Token/cost totals are critical for users tracking spend. Paging through history and seeing "-" for every row makes the history view less useful.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13971 (fix(desktop): show token usage and cost for every visible session-history page)
- **Category**: command (desktop UI, session listing)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi has no desktop app, no session-history pagination UI. This is desktop-specific. Not CLI-portable. If Alexi adds a TUI session-list view with pagination in the future, consider on-demand usage hydration for visible pages.
